GDP at current prices, not inflation-adjusted.
GDP ÷ population — average output per person.
% increase in real GDP over time.

walkthroughs.body_html: GDP is the total value of all goods and services produced in a country in a year. Three ways to calculate: output, income or expenditure — all give the same answer in theory. UK GDP ~£2.5 trillion (2024).

Nominal uses current prices — can rise just because prices rose. Real strips out inflation, showing genuine output change. If nominal grows 5% but inflation is 3%, real growth is only 2%. Always use real GDP to compare years.
1) Boom — rapid growth, low unemployment, rising inflation. 2) Recession — two quarters of falling GDP. 3) Slump/trough — bottom. 4) Recovery — growth restarts. Cycles last ~5–10 years on average.
